words.enDefinition: Repeatable procedure whose particular outcome is uncertain before it is performed

examples.en: The random experiment consists of drawing one numbered tile from a thoroughly mixed bag.
examples.zh: 这个「随机试验」是从充分混合的袋子中抽出一块编号牌。

examples.en: We described each possible result before carrying out the random experiment in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂进行「随机试验」前，先描述了每一种可能的结果。

words.enDefinition: Set containing all possible outcomes of the random procedure being modeled

examples.en: The sample space for two labeled dice contains ordered pairs of possible face values.
examples.zh: 两枚有标记骰子的「样本空间」由可能点数构成的有序对组成。

examples.en: We changed the sample space when the exercise began recording colors instead of numbers.
examples.zh: 习题改为记录颜色后，我们也调整了「样本空间」。

words.enDefinition: Set of possible outcomes containing only a finite number of elements

examples.en: Our finite sample space contains six outcomes because it records one die's top face.
examples.zh: 我们的「有限样本空间」有六个结果，因为它记录一枚骰子朝上的点数。

examples.en: We verified that the probabilities across the finite sample space added up to one.
examples.zh: 我们验证了这个「有限样本空间」内各结果的概率之和为一。

collocations: count outcomes in a finite sample space

words.enDefinition: Infinite outcome set whose elements can be listed in a sequence

examples.en: Counting tosses until the first head gives a countably infinite sample space in our model.
examples.zh: 在我们的模型中，数出首次出现正面所需的抛掷次数，得到的是「可数无穷样本空间」。

examples.en: We represented the countably infinite sample space using the positive integers and one additional outcome.
examples.zh: 我们用正整数加上一个额外结果来表示「可数无穷样本空间」。

collocations: construct a countably infinite sample space
use a countably infinite sample space
probability on a countably infinite sample space

words.enDefinition: Single possible result that is an element of the modeled outcome set

examples.en: The ordered pair showing two threes is one elementary outcome in our dice model.
examples.zh: 在我们的骰子模型里，表示两个三点的有序对是一个「基本结果」。

examples.en: We assigned a probability to each elementary outcome before grouping outcomes into events.
examples.zh: 我们先给每个「基本结果」赋予一个概率，再把结果归入事件。

collocations: assign a probability to an elementary outcome

words.enDefinition: Event containing exactly one outcome from the chosen sample space

examples.en: In this model, rolling exactly two is a simple event with one possible outcome.
examples.zh: 在这个模型中，恰好掷出两点是一个「简单事件」，只包含一个可能结果。

examples.en: We used braces to represent the simple event containing the single possible outcome.
examples.zh: 我们用花括号表示只包含一个可能结果的「简单事件」。

words.enDefinition: Event containing multiple elementary outcomes in the model being studied

examples.en: Rolling an even number is a compound event that contains three die outcomes.
examples.zh: 掷出偶数是一个「复合事件」，包含三个骰子结果。

examples.en: We listed the outcomes in the compound event before calculating its probability.
examples.zh: 求这个「复合事件」的概率之前，我们列出了它包含的结果。

words.enDefinition: Possible results all assigned the same probability under the chosen model

examples.en: A fair die has six equally likely outcomes when we record its top face.
examples.zh: 如果记录朝上的点数，一枚公平骰子有六种「等可能结果」。

examples.en: We used equally likely outcomes only after checking the symmetry assumed in the problem.
examples.zh: 核对题目所假设的对称性后，我们才采用「等可能结果」。

words.enDefinition: Event including every outcome in the model and therefore always occurring

examples.en: A result from one through six is a certain event in our dice experiment.
examples.zh: 在我们的骰子试验中，掷出一到六的数是一个「必然事件」。

examples.en: We gave the certain event probability one because it included the entire sample space.
examples.zh: 由于它包含整个样本空间，我们把「必然事件」的概率设为一。

words.enDefinition: Event containing no outcomes under the stated rules of the experiment

examples.en: Drawing a blue tile is an impossible event when the bag contains only red tiles.
examples.zh: 袋中只有红牌时，抽到蓝牌是「不可能事件」。

examples.en: The impossible event is represented by the empty set in our model.
examples.zh: 在我们的模型中，「不可能事件」用空集表示。

words.enDefinition: Event assigned probability zero even if it contains possible outcomes

examples.en: In the continuous model, obtaining exactly five is a zero-probability event with one possible value.
examples.zh: 在该连续模型中，恰好取五是一个含有一种可能取值的「零概率事件」。

examples.en: An interval of positive length had positive probability, while its endpoint formed a zero-probability event.
examples.zh: 一个有正长度的区间在该例中概率为正，其中一个端点对应「零概率事件」。

words.enDefinition: Event consisting of every outcome outside the original event

examples.en: For totals of at least eight, the event complement contains all outcomes with totals below eight.
examples.zh: 对于点数和至少为八的事件，其「事件的补集」包含点数和小于八的所有结果。

examples.en: The event complement includes the outcomes left unshaded in our sample space diagram.
examples.zh: 我们样本空间图上没有阴影的结果属于「事件的补集」。

words.enDefinition: Rule finding an event's probability by subtracting its complement's probability from one

examples.en: Using the complement rule, we found the chance of seeing at least one head.
examples.zh: 我们用「补事件法则」求出了出现至少一个正面的概率。

examples.en: The complement rule made the problem easier because the opposite event had fewer outcomes.
examples.zh: 由于相反事件包含的结果更少，「补事件法则」让题目更容易计算。

words.enDefinition: Events sharing no outcomes and therefore unable to occur together

examples.en: The worksheet treats drawing red and drawing blue as mutually exclusive events on a single draw.
examples.zh: 在单次抽取时，习题把抽到红色和抽到蓝色视为「互斥事件」。

examples.en: Our two events cannot happen together, so we classified them as mutually exclusive events.
examples.zh: 这两个事件不能同时发生，所以我们把它们划为「互斥事件」。

collocations: mutually exclusive events in one trial

words.enDefinition: Collection of events whose members together cover the whole sample space

examples.en: Each possible roll lies in at least one listed event, making them collectively exhaustive events.
examples.zh: 每种可能的掷骰结果至少属于一个所列事件，因此这些事件构成「穷尽事件组」。

examples.en: We found collectively exhaustive events that could overlap while still covering all possible outcomes.
examples.zh: 我们找到了一个「穷尽事件组」，其中各事件可以重叠，同时涵盖全部可能结果。

words.enDefinition: Collection of disjoint nonempty events covering every possible outcome exactly once

examples.en: Grouping rolls into even and odd outcomes gives a partition of the sample space in our example.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，将掷骰结果按奇偶分组，就形成了「样本空间的划分」。

examples.en: We used a partition of the sample space so each possible result belonged to exactly one group.
examples.zh: 我们对「样本空间进行划分」，使每一种可能的结果都恰好属于一个组。

collocations: form a partition of the sample space
choose a partition of the sample space
check a partition of the sample space

words.enDefinition: Upper bound on a union's probability given by summing the individual probabilities

examples.en: We used the union bound to bound the chance that at least one event occurred.
examples.zh: 我们用「并集概率上界」给至少发生一个事件的概率定出上界。

examples.en: The union bound stays valid even when some of the events can happen together.
examples.zh: 即使部分事件可以同时发生，「并集概率上界」仍然成立。

collocations: estimate a probability using the union bound

words.enDefinition: Probability that two or more specified events occur together

examples.en: We found the joint probability of drawing a large tile that was also blue.
examples.zh: 我们求出了既抽到大牌又抽到蓝牌的「联合概率」。

examples.en: The table gives joint probability for each combination of color and shape in the bag.
examples.zh: 表中给出了袋中每种颜色和形状组合对应的「联合概率」。

words.enDefinition: Probability of one event obtained without restricting the other outcomes or variables

examples.en: We found the marginal probability of blue by including all shapes in that color.
examples.zh: 我们把这种颜色的所有形状都算上，求出了蓝色的「边缘概率」。

examples.en: The marginal probability in the table can be read by summing across one row.
examples.zh: 把表中一行的各项相加，就能得到对应的「边缘概率」。

collocations: find a marginal probability by summing

words.enDefinition: Probability of an event given that specified information or another event holds

examples.en: We calculated the conditional probability of an even number given that it exceeded three.
examples.zh: 在已知点数大于三的条件下，我们计算了点数为偶数的「条件概率」。

examples.en: The conditional probability changed when the tutor revealed which bag supplied the tile.
examples.zh: 老师揭示牌抽自哪个袋子后，「条件概率」改变了。

words.enDefinition: Rule adding individual probabilities and removing double counting for overlapping events

examples.en: Using the addition rule of probability, we subtracted the probability of outcomes counted in both events.
examples.zh: 使用「概率加法法则」时，我们减去了在两个事件中均被计入的结果的概率。

examples.en: The addition rule of probability reduced to a sum because the two groups did not overlap.
examples.zh: 因为两组结果没有重叠，「概率加法法则」简化为直接相加。

collocations: apply the addition rule of probability
use the addition rule of probability
state the addition rule of probability

words.enDefinition: Rule multiplying one event's probability by the other's probability conditional on it

examples.en: We used the multiplication rule of probability after finding the probability of blue given an initial red draw.
examples.zh: 求出在第一次抽到红牌的条件下接着抽到蓝牌的概率后，我们使用了「概率乘法法则」。

examples.en: The multiplication rule of probability works here even though the two draws are dependent.
examples.zh: 尽管两次抽取并不独立，「概率乘法法则」在这里仍然适用。

collocations: apply the multiplication rule of probability
use the multiplication rule of probability
derive the multiplication rule of probability

words.enDefinition: Rule adding conditional probabilities weighted by the probabilities of partition events

examples.en: We used the law of total probability to combine the chances of blue from two possible bags.
examples.zh: 我们用「全概率公式」综合计算从两个可能的袋子中抽到蓝牌的概率。

examples.en: The law of total probability weights each conditional chance by the probability of choosing its bag.
examples.zh: 「全概率公式」用每个袋子被选中的概率为对应的条件概率加权。

collocations: apply the law of total probability
use the law of total probability
derive the law of total probability

words.enDefinition: Formula reversing a conditioning direction using prior probabilities and conditional evidence

examples.en: We applied Bayes' theorem to infer the bag given the color of the tile.
examples.zh: 我们应用「贝叶斯定理」，根据牌的颜色推断它来自哪个袋子。

examples.en: The tutor used Bayes' theorem to reverse which event the problem conditions on.
examples.zh: 老师用「贝叶斯定理」调换了题目中作为条件的事件和要求概率的事件。

collocations: solve a problem using Bayes' theorem

words.enDefinition: Probability assigned to a hypothesis before the specified evidence is taken into account

examples.en: The prior probability of choosing the first bag comes from the original selection rule.
examples.zh: 选择第一个袋子的「先验概率」由最初的选择规则给出。

examples.en: We wrote the prior probability before looking at the color of the selected tile.
examples.zh: 我们在看抽中的牌的颜色之前，先写下了「先验概率」。

words.enDefinition: Probability of a hypothesis conditional on the evidence that has been observed

examples.en: The posterior probability favored the larger bag after we observed a red tile.
examples.zh: 看到一块红牌后，「后验概率」显示牌来自较大袋子的可能性更高。

examples.en: We compared the posterior probability with its original value before seeing the evidence.
examples.zh: 我们将「后验概率」与看到这一证据前的概率作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Overall probability or frequency of an event before conditioning on extra information

examples.en: The base rate of blue tiles was low before any shape was observed.
examples.zh: 看到任何形状信息之前，蓝色牌的「基准发生率」很低。

examples.en: Our example compares the base rate with the rate among tiles marked as large.
examples.zh: 我们的例子把「基准发生率」和大号牌中的发生率作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Error of neglecting the overall frequency when interpreting evidence about an event

examples.en: Our tile example illustrates the base-rate fallacy when students ignore how rare blue is.
examples.zh: 在我们的牌类示例中，学生忽略蓝牌很少这件事，体现了「基率谬误」。

examples.en: The tutor used a table of frequencies to explain the base-rate fallacy in class.
examples.zh: 老师在课堂上用一张频数表说明了「基率谬误」。

words.enDefinition: Events for which joint probabilities factor into products of individual probabilities

examples.en: In our model, heads on the first toss and heads on the second are independent events.
examples.zh: 在我们的模型中，第一次抛出正面与第二次抛出正面是「独立事件」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks whether the events are independent events before multiplying their probabilities.
examples.zh: 习题要求先判断这对事件是否为「独立事件」，再相乘它们的概率。

collocations: distinguish independent events from disjoint events

words.enDefinition: Product factorization of probabilities after fixing the stated conditioning information

examples.en: We assumed conditional independence between the draws after fixing which bag was used.
examples.zh: 我们在确定使用哪个袋子后，假定两次抽取满足「条件独立」。

examples.en: The model assumes conditional independence for two readings given the same fixed temperature.
examples.zh: 给定同一个固定温度后，模型假设两次读数满足「条件独立」。

words.enDefinition: Independence of each pair within a specified family of events

examples.en: To check pairwise independence, we compared each pair's joint probability with the product of its probabilities.
examples.zh: 为检查「两两独立」，我们将每一对事件的联合概率与各自概率的乘积作了比较。

examples.en: Our example shows pairwise independence even though the probability of all three fails to factor.
examples.zh: 尽管三个事件同时发生的概率不能分解为各自概率的乘积，本例中仍有「两两独立」。

words.enDefinition: Full independence requiring probability factorization for every subset of the event family

examples.en: We checked probabilities for triples as well as pairs before claiming mutual independence.
examples.zh: 我们核对了三项组合以及两项组合的概率，才断定存在「相互独立」。

examples.en: Under mutual independence, the joint probability factors for any selected group of events.
examples.zh: 在「相互独立」下，任意选定一组事件的联合概率都可以分解为各自概率的乘积。

words.enDefinition: Repeated trials whose outcomes are mutually independent, so joint probabilities factor across the trials.

examples.en: The worksheet models each repeated spin as one of several independent trials.
examples.zh: 习题把每次重复转动建模为多次「独立试验」中的一次。

examples.en: We used independent trials so the previous result did not change the next probabilities.
examples.zh: 我们采用「独立试验」，使前一次结果不改变下一次的概率。

words.enDefinition: Drawing repeatedly from a population while returning selected items before subsequent draws

examples.en: With sampling with replacement, the same numbered tile can appear on two consecutive draws.
examples.zh: 采用「放回抽样」时，同一块编号牌可能连续两次被抽到。

examples.en: The class used sampling with replacement to keep the contents of the bag unchanged between draws.
examples.zh: 全班采用「放回抽样」，让袋中物品在两次抽取之间保持不变。

collocations: sampling with replacement from a bag

words.enDefinition: Drawing repeatedly from a population while leaving selected items out of later draws

examples.en: Under sampling without replacement, a tile removed on the first draw cannot appear again.
examples.zh: 采用「不放回抽样」时，第一次抽出并取走的牌不能再次出现。

examples.en: We modeled sampling without replacement to allow the second probability to depend on the first result.
examples.zh: 我们对「不放回抽样」建模，让第二次的概率可以取决于第一次的结果。

collocations: sampling without replacement from a bag

words.enDefinition: Rule multiplying option counts for successive stages with fixed counts at each stage

examples.en: We used the fundamental counting principle to count outfits made from one shirt and one hat.
examples.zh: 我们用「乘法计数原理」计算由一件衬衫和一顶帽子组成的搭配数。

examples.en: The fundamental counting principle gives twelve choices when three options can each pair with four others.
examples.zh: 三种选项中的每一种都能搭配另四种选项时，「乘法计数原理」给出十二种选择。

collocations: example of the fundamental counting principle

words.enDefinition: Rule adding the numbers of options from separate, nonoverlapping cases

examples.en: We used the addition principle of counting after splitting the choices into two disjoint groups.
examples.zh: 我们把选项拆成两个不相交的组后，应用了「加法计数原理」。

examples.en: The addition principle of counting counts shirts and coats when the problem asks for one item.
examples.zh: 当题目要求只选一件物品时，「加法计数原理」将可选衬衫数和外套数相加。

collocations: apply the addition principle of counting
use the addition principle of counting
illustrate the addition principle of counting

words.enDefinition: Counting rule alternating additions and subtractions to correct for overlapping sets

examples.en: We used the inclusion-exclusion principle to count tiles with at least one of three features.
examples.zh: 我们用「容斥原理」计算符合三项特征中至少一项的牌的数量。

examples.en: The inclusion-exclusion principle added back the triple intersection after subtracting the three pairwise overlaps.
examples.zh: 在减去三组两两重叠的数量后，「容斥原理」又加回了三组共同重叠的数量。

words.enDefinition: Ordered arrangement of selected elements from the given collection

examples.en: Changing the first two letters gives a different permutation in this example.
examples.zh: 在这个例子中，调换前两个字母就得到一种不同的「排列」。

examples.en: We listed each permutation of the three labeled books on the shelf.
examples.zh: 我们列出了书架上三本有标记的书可能出现的每种「排列」。

words.enDefinition: Distinct orderings of a collection containing indistinguishable copies of some elements

examples.en: We divided by two when counting permutations with repeated elements because two letters were identical.
examples.zh: 计算「有重复元素的排列」时，由于两个字母相同，我们把排列数除以二。

examples.en: The worksheet uses permutations with repeated elements to count the possible orders of identical colored tiles.
examples.zh: 习题用「有重复元素的排列」统计有些牌颜色相同的情况下各种可能顺序。

collocations: formula for permutations with repeated elements

words.enDefinition: Number of ways to choose a fixed-size subset from a finite set

examples.en: We used a binomial coefficient to count pairs selected from the six numbered tiles.
examples.zh: 我们用「二项式系数」计算从六块编号牌中选出两块的选法。

examples.en: The binomial coefficient stays the same when we interchange chosen and unchosen objects.
examples.zh: 把选中的物品与未选中的物品互换时，「二项式系数」不变。

words.enDefinition: Number of assignments of distinct objects to labeled groups of specified sizes

examples.en: The multinomial coefficient counts ways to assign six students to three labeled teams of two.
examples.zh: 「多项式系数」计算了把六名学生分到三个有标记、每组两人的小队的分法。

examples.en: We used a multinomial coefficient with the three group size factorials in the denominator.
examples.zh: 我们采用「多项式系数」，在分母写出三个组各自人数的阶乘。

collocations: count arrangements using a multinomial coefficient

words.enDefinition: Choice of elements in which rearranging the selected items changes nothing

examples.en: The tutor treated choosing two volunteers as an unordered selection because they shared one role.
examples.zh: 因为两名志愿者承担同样的角色，老师把选出这两人视为「无序选择」。

examples.en: We counted each unordered selection once even if the objects could be listed differently.
examples.zh: 即使物品可以按不同顺序列出，我们对每种「无序选择」也只计一次。

words.enDefinition: Exclamation mark after an integer denoting multiplication of all positive integers through it

examples.en: We wrote the descending product in factorial notation before simplifying the counting expression.
examples.zh: 化简计数式之前，我们先用「阶乘记号」写出连乘式。

examples.en: The tutor explained how factorial notation shortens the formula for a binomial coefficient.
examples.zh: 老师解释了「阶乘记号」如何使二项式系数的公式更简洁。

collocations: write a product in factorial notation

words.enDefinition: Numerical function assigning a value to each possible outcome of an experiment

examples.en: The random variable counts how many heads appear when we toss three coins.
examples.zh: 「随机变量」记录抛三枚硬币时出现正面的次数。

examples.en: We defined a random variable that assigns a number to each colored tile.
examples.zh: 我们定义了一个「随机变量」，给每块彩色牌对应一个数值。

words.enDefinition: Random quantity taking values in a finite or countably infinite set

examples.en: The number of heads is a discrete random variable taking only whole numbers here.
examples.zh: 在这里，出现正面的次数是一个只取整数值的「离散随机变量」。

examples.en: We gave the discrete random variable a separate probability for each of its possible values.
examples.zh: 我们为该「离散随机变量」的每个可能取值分别赋予了一个概率。

collocations: distribution of a discrete random variable

words.enDefinition: Random quantity modeled by a probability density over real-valued intervals

examples.en: The model treats waiting time as a continuous random variable measured to arbitrary precision.
examples.zh: 模型把等待时间视为可以任意精确地测量的「连续随机变量」。

examples.en: For a continuous random variable, the area over an interval gives its probability here.
examples.zh: 在这里，已知「连续随机变量」的密度，区间上方的面积就给出该区间的概率。

collocations: density of a continuous random variable

words.enDefinition: Specification of how probability is allocated across the values of a variable

examples.en: We wrote the probability distribution for the count of heads in three tosses.
examples.zh: 我们写出了三次抛掷中正面出现次数的「概率分布」。

examples.en: The probability distribution changed after we switched from counts to waiting times in class.
examples.zh: 在课堂中，我们从次数改为等待时间后，「概率分布」发生了变化。

words.enDefinition: Distribution having both positive point probabilities and a part described by density

examples.en: Our mixed distribution places some probability at zero and spreads the rest over positive values.
examples.zh: 我们的「混合型分布」将部分概率集中在零，将其余概率分布在正值上。

examples.en: We used a mixed distribution because some people started waiting while others entered immediately.
examples.zh: 有些人开始等待，其他人立即进入，所以我们采用「混合型分布」。

collocations: continuous component of a mixed distribution

words.enDefinition: Probability distribution assigning all its probability to a single value

examples.en: The degenerate distribution assigns probability one to the only value in the model.
examples.zh: 在该模型中，「退化分布」将概率一赋予唯一的取值。

examples.en: Our example has a degenerate distribution because the variable always equals the same number.
examples.zh: 因为变量始终等于同一个数，我们的例子具有「退化分布」。

words.enDefinition: Smallest closed set containing a variable's value with probability one

examples.en: We read the support of a distribution from the values with positive probabilities in the discrete table.
examples.zh: 我们从离散分布表中概率为正的取值读出了「分布的支撑集」。

examples.en: The support of a distribution consists of the nonnegative integers in the example we discussed.
examples.zh: 在我们讨论的例子里，「分布的支撑集」由非负整数组成。

collocations: find the support of a distribution
specify the support of a distribution
describe the support of a distribution

words.enDefinition: Fixed number identifying a particular member of a family of distributions

examples.en: The distribution parameter determines the success chance in our repeated coin toss model.
examples.zh: 在我们重复抛硬币的模型中，「分布参数」决定成功的概率。

examples.en: We changed one distribution parameter while keeping the rest of the model fixed.
examples.zh: 我们改变了一个「分布参数」，其余模型部分保持不变。

words.enDefinition: Function giving the probability of each individual value of a discrete variable

examples.en: We checked that the values of the probability mass function summed to one in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们检查了习题中的「概率质量函数」各个值的总和是否为一。

examples.en: The probability mass function assigns larger values to middle counts in this example.
examples.zh: 在这个例子中，「概率质量函数」为中间的计数赋予了更高的概率。

words.enDefinition: Nonnegative function whose integral gives probabilities over intervals for a continuous variable

examples.en: We integrated the probability density function between two times to find the chance of waiting that long.
examples.zh: 我们在两个时刻之间对「概率密度函数」积分，求出等待时间落在两者之间的概率。

examples.en: The probability density function reaches above one here, but its total area is one.
examples.zh: 这里的「概率密度函数」取值超过一，但总面积为一。

words.enDefinition: Function giving the probability that a variable is at most a specified value

examples.en: The cumulative distribution function gives the chance of waiting no more than ten minutes.
examples.zh: 「累积分布函数」给出了等待时间不超过十分钟的概率。

examples.en: We observed a jump in the cumulative distribution function at a value with positive probability.
examples.zh: 我们发现，某个取值的概率为正时，「累积分布函数」在该取值处出现跳跃。

collocations: jump in the cumulative distribution function

words.enDefinition: Total probability that the variable does not exceed a specified threshold

examples.en: We found the cumulative probability up to three by adding probabilities for counts of three or less.
examples.zh: 我们把不超过三的各个计数对应的概率相加，得到截至三的「累积概率」。

examples.en: The table gives cumulative probability at each distance measured from the starting point.
examples.zh: 这张表给出了距离起点不超过各列距离时的「累积概率」。

collocations: cumulative probability up to a threshold

words.enDefinition: Positive probability assigned to one particular value in a distribution

examples.en: The distribution has a point mass at zero because some arrivals wait no time.
examples.zh: 分布在零处有「点质量」，因为一些到达者无需等待。

examples.en: The jump in the cumulative distribution function equals the point mass at that value.
examples.zh: 累积分布函数在该取值处的跳跃大小等于这里的「点质量」。

words.enDefinition: Probability lying beyond a specified cutoff on one side of a distribution

examples.en: We found the tail probability above ten by subtracting the cumulative probability from one.
examples.zh: 我们用一减去累积概率，求得大于十的「尾部概率」。

examples.en: The graph shades the tail probability to the left of the selected cutoff.
examples.zh: 这张图用阴影表示选定界值左侧的「尾部概率」。

words.enDefinition: Probability law describing the outcomes of two or more variables considered together

examples.en: The joint distribution gives a probability for each possible combination of chair color and size.
examples.zh: 「联合分布」为椅子颜色和尺寸的每种可能组合给出一个概率。

examples.en: We found the joint distribution of two counts obtained from the same experiment.
examples.zh: 我们求出了同一试验所得两个计数的「联合分布」。

words.enDefinition: Distribution of selected variables obtained by summing or integrating over the others

examples.en: We summed across colors to get the marginal distribution of tile size.
examples.zh: 我们对各种颜色求和，得到了牌大小的「边缘分布」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks for the marginal distribution of one variable from the joint density.
examples.zh: 习题要求根据联合密度求出一个变量的「边缘分布」。

collocations: calculate a marginal distribution from a joint table

words.enDefinition: Probability distribution of a variable given another value or specified information

examples.en: We compared the conditional distribution of tile sizes after being told which color was drawn.
examples.zh: 得知抽中的颜色之后，我们比较了牌大小的「条件分布」。

examples.en: The conditional distribution in the second row uses only outcomes from the large bag.
examples.zh: 第二行的「条件分布」只使用来自大袋子的结果。

words.enDefinition: Function assigning probabilities to combinations of values of several discrete variables

examples.en: The joint probability mass function gives one probability for each pair of observed counts.
examples.zh: 「联合概率质量函数」为每对观测计数给出一个概率。

examples.en: We summed the joint probability mass function over all possible pairs to check its normalization.
examples.zh: 我们在所有可能数对上对「联合概率质量函数」求和，检查它是否归一。

collocations: write the joint probability mass function
sum a joint probability mass function
calculate the joint probability mass function

words.enDefinition: Function whose integral over a region gives the probability of variable combinations

examples.en: We integrated the joint probability density function over a rectangle to find its probability.
examples.zh: 我们在一个矩形区域上对「联合概率密度函数」积分，求出了落在该区域内的概率。

examples.en: The joint probability density function is zero outside the triangle drawn on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 在习题所画的三角形之外，「联合概率密度函数」为零。

collocations: write a joint probability density function
integrate a joint probability density function
support of a joint probability density function

words.enDefinition: Sum or integrate out uncertain values to obtain a distribution of remaining variables

examples.en: To find the distribution of tile size, we marginalize over the observed colors.
examples.zh: 为求出牌大小的分布，我们「对所观测的颜色变量边缘化」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks us to marginalize over one variable using an integral.
examples.zh: 习题要求我们用积分「对一个变量进行边缘化」。

words.enDefinition: Variables whose joint distribution factors into the product of their marginal distributions

examples.en: Our model uses independent random variables for counts from two separate runs of the experiment.
examples.zh: 我们的模型用「独立随机变量」表示来自两轮独立试验的计数。

examples.en: We used independent random variables so knowing one variable did not change the other's distribution.
examples.zh: 我们采用「独立随机变量」，使知道一个变量的取值不改变另一个变量的分布。

words.enDefinition: Variables having the same marginal distribution regardless of whether dependence exists

examples.en: The worksheet uses identically distributed random variables for repeated counts with the same probability law.
examples.zh: 这道题用「同分布随机变量」表示服从同一概率分布的多个计数。

examples.en: These are identically distributed random variables even though the second value copies the first in our model.
examples.zh: 我们模型里第二个变量始终与第一个变量取相同的值，因此两者是「同分布随机变量」。

collocations: sequence of identically distributed random variables

words.enDefinition: Mutually independent and all having the same probability distribution

examples.en: Our model assumes the repeated counts are independent and identically distributed throughout the experiment.
examples.zh: 我们模型假定整个试验中重复得到的计数都是「独立同分布的」。

examples.en: The tutor checked whether the simulated waiting times were independent and identically distributed before applying the theorem.
examples.zh: 老师在应用定理之前，检查了模拟等待时间是否都是「独立同分布的」。

collocations: assume independent and identically distributed variables

words.enDefinition: Operation giving the distribution of a sum of independent random variables

examples.en: We used the convolution of distributions to find the distribution of the sum of two independent counts.
examples.zh: 我们用「分布的卷积」求出了两个独立计数之和的分布。

examples.en: The exercise calculates a convolution of distributions by summing over all ways to reach each total.
examples.zh: 这道题对每个总数的所有组成方式求和，计算了「分布的卷积」。

words.enDefinition: Probability-weighted average of possible numerical values under the chosen distribution

examples.en: The expected value of a single fair die roll is not itself a possible outcome.
examples.zh: 掷一枚公平骰子所得点数的「期望值」本身不是一个可能掷出的点数。

examples.en: We multiplied each value by its probability before adding to find the expected value.
examples.zh: 我们把各个数值分别乘以其概率，再相加求得「期望值」。

collocations: expected value of a random variable

words.enDefinition: Probability-weighted average calculated under the distribution implied by given information

examples.en: The conditional expectation changed after the tutor revealed the first outcome in the experiment.
examples.zh: 老师揭示试验中的第一个结果之后，「条件期望」发生了变化。

examples.en: We found the conditional expectation of the count given that the first toss landed heads.
examples.zh: 已知第一次抛出正面时，我们求出了计数的「条件期望」。

words.enDefinition: Property making the expectation of a weighted sum equal the weighted expectations

examples.en: We used linearity of expectation to add the means even though the counts were dependent.
examples.zh: 即使这几个计数并不独立，我们也用「期望的线性性质」将期望值相加。

examples.en: The linearity of expectation lets us move the constant multiplier outside the expectation.
examples.zh: 利用「期望的线性性质」，我们可以把常数因子提到期望运算之外。

words.enDefinition: Identity obtaining an overall expectation by averaging conditional expectations with appropriate weights

examples.en: We used the law of total expectation to average the expected wait across both queues.
examples.zh: 我们用「全期望公式」求出了综合两个队列的平均期望等待时间。

examples.en: The law of total expectation weights each group's conditional mean by its overall probability.
examples.zh: 「全期望公式」按各组的总体概率为其条件均值加权。

collocations: apply the law of total expectation
use the law of total expectation
derive the law of total expectation

words.enDefinition: Expected squared difference between a variable and its own mean

examples.en: We found the variance of a random variable by averaging squared deviations using their probabilities.
examples.zh: 我们以概率加权计算平方偏差的平均值，求出了「随机变量的方差」。

examples.en: The variance of a random variable is zero when its value never changes across outcomes.
examples.zh: 如果变量在所有结果中始终取同一个值，「随机变量的方差」就是零。

collocations: calculate the variance of a random variable
compare the variance of a random variable
formula for the variance of a random variable

words.enDefinition: Nonnegative square root of the variance, expressed in the variable's units

examples.en: The standard deviation of a distribution has the same units as waiting time in our exercise.
examples.zh: 在我们的习题中，「分布的标准差」与等待时间使用相同的单位。

examples.en: We took a square root to recover the standard deviation of a distribution from its variance.
examples.zh: 我们将方差开平方，得到「分布的标准差」。

collocations: calculate the standard deviation of a distribution
compare the standard deviation of a distribution
interpret the standard deviation of a distribution

words.enDefinition: Variance computed using the distribution that remains after conditioning on specified information

examples.en: We computed the conditional variance of waiting time after fixing which queue the visitor joined.
examples.zh: 我们先确定访客排的是哪个队列，再计算等待时间的「条件方差」。

examples.en: The conditional variance is smaller in one group even though its mean is higher.
examples.zh: 其中一组虽然均值更高，但「条件方差」更小。

collocations: law of total variance using conditional variance

words.enDefinition: Variance of combined variables, accounting for each variance and pairwise covariance

examples.en: For independent variables, we calculated the variance of a sum by adding their individual variances.
examples.zh: 对于独立变量，我们将各自的方差相加，得到「和的方差」。

examples.en: The variance of a sum included a positive covariance term for the two related measurements.
examples.zh: 这两个相关的测量值有正协方差，因此计算「和的方差」时包含一项正的协方差贡献。

collocations: calculate the variance of a sum
variance of a sum of independent variables
formula for the variance of a sum

words.enDefinition: Identity splitting variance into average conditional variance and variance of conditional means

examples.en: We applied the law of total variance to distinguish variation within queues from differences between queue means.
examples.zh: 我们用「全方差公式」区分各队列内部的变异和队列平均值之间的差异。

examples.en: The law of total variance requires both the expected within-group variance and the variation of group means.
examples.zh: 「全方差公式」既需要组内方差的期望，也需要组均值的方差。

collocations: apply the law of total variance
derive the law of total variance
use the law of total variance

words.enDefinition: Expected product of the deviations of two variables from their means

examples.en: The covariance is positive because large values of the two counts tend to occur together.
examples.zh: 两个计数的较大值往往同时出现，所以「协方差」为正。

examples.en: We calculated covariance after subtracting the corresponding mean from each variable.
examples.zh: 我们从各变量中减去相应的均值，再计算「协方差」。

words.enDefinition: Covariance divided by the product of two positive standard deviations

examples.en: We scaled the covariance by both standard deviations to find the correlation coefficient.
examples.zh: 我们用两个标准差的乘积作除数，对协方差进行缩放，求出「相关系数」。

examples.en: The correlation coefficient does not change when we convert both lengths to centimeters.
examples.zh: 当我们把两个长度变量都换算成厘米时，「相关系数」保持不变。

words.enDefinition: Variables with finite second moments and covariance equal to zero

examples.en: The example shows uncorrelated random variables that still depend on each other in a nonlinear way.
examples.zh: 例子展示了以非线性方式相互依赖的「不相关随机变量」。

examples.en: We classified the pair as uncorrelated random variables after calculating their covariance exactly.
examples.zh: 准确计算这两个变量的协方差后，我们将它们归为「不相关随机变量」。

collocations: distinguish uncorrelated random variables from independent ones

words.enDefinition: Expected value of a specified power of an uncentered random variable

examples.en: We calculated the second raw moment by taking the expected value of the squared variable.
examples.zh: 我们对变量的平方取期望，求得二阶「原点矩」。

examples.en: The exercise uses a raw moment to derive a formula for the variance.
examples.zh: 习题用一个「原点矩」推导出方差公式。

words.enDefinition: Expected power of a variable's deviation from its own mean

examples.en: The variance is the second central moment of the distribution in our example.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，方差是分布的二阶「中心矩」。

examples.en: We subtracted the mean before cubing the values for the third central moment.
examples.zh: 我们先减去均值，再将所得偏差立方，以求三阶「中心矩」。

words.enDefinition: Expectation of an exponential of a variable times an argument, where finite

examples.en: We differentiated the moment-generating function at zero to recover the first moment.
examples.zh: 我们在零处对「矩生成函数」求导，得到一阶原点矩。

examples.en: The tutor multiplied two functions to obtain the moment-generating function of their independent sum.
examples.zh: 老师把两个函数相乘，求得两个独立变量之和的「矩生成函数」。

words.enDefinition: Expected power of the argument with a nonnegative integer variable as exponent

examples.en: The coefficients of the probability generating function give the probabilities for the possible counts.
examples.zh: 「概率生成函数」的各个系数给出了各可能计数的概率。

examples.en: We evaluated the probability generating function at one to check that its coefficients summed correctly.
examples.zh: 我们在一处求「概率生成函数」的值，核查各系数之和是否正确。

collocations: probability generating function for a count

words.enDefinition: For a probability level strictly between zero and one, the smallest value at which the cumulative distribution reaches or exceeds that level.

examples.en: The worksheet asks for the distribution quantile corresponding to cumulative probability of three quarters.
examples.zh: 习题要求求出累积概率为四分之三所对应的「分布分位数」。

examples.en: We read the distribution quantile from the horizontal axis after locating its probability level.
examples.zh: 我们先找到该概率水平，再从横轴上读出「分布分位数」。

words.enDefinition: Function assigning a distribution cutoff to each specified cumulative probability level

examples.en: We evaluated the quantile function at one half to find the model's median.
examples.zh: 我们把二分之一代入「分位数函数」，求出了模型的中位数。

examples.en: The quantile function converts the chosen probability level into a cutoff on the original scale.
examples.zh: 「分位数函数」把所选的概率水平转换为原量表上的界值。

collocations: invert the cumulative distribution to obtain a quantile function

words.enDefinition: Probability distribution that remains unchanged when reflected around its central point

examples.en: The symmetric distribution gives the same probability to equally wide ranges on opposite sides.
examples.zh: 在中心两侧相同位置的等宽区间内，「对称分布」赋予的概率相同。

examples.en: We drew a symmetric distribution by reflecting the left half across its vertical center line.
examples.zh: 我们将左半部分沿其中心竖线作镜像，画出了一个「对称分布」。

words.enDefinition: Distribution with a longer tail on its high-value side

examples.en: Our right-skewed distribution has many brief waits and a few much longer ones.
examples.zh: 我们的「右偏分布」中，短等待时间很多，较长的等待时间只有少数。

examples.en: We sketched a right-skewed distribution with its tail extending toward larger values.
examples.zh: 我们画了一个尾部向较大数值延伸的「右偏分布」。

collocations: long tail of a right-skewed distribution

words.enDefinition: Distribution with a longer tail on its low-value side

examples.en: The left-skewed distribution has most of its values near the top of the scale.
examples.zh: 这个「左偏分布」的大多数值都接近量表上端。

examples.en: We drew a left-skewed distribution with a few unusually small values stretching its left tail.
examples.zh: 我们画出了一个「左偏分布」，其中少数异常小的值使左尾拉长。

collocations: long tail of a left-skewed distribution

words.enDefinition: Distribution assigning equal probability to each value of a finite set

examples.en: The model uses a discrete uniform distribution for the face of a fair die.
examples.zh: 模型用「离散均匀分布」表示公平骰子朝上的点数。

examples.en: We calculated the mean of a discrete uniform distribution on five equally likely numbers.
examples.zh: 我们计算了在五个等可能数字上的「离散均匀分布」的均值。

collocations: sample from a discrete uniform distribution

words.enDefinition: Distribution having constant density over a bounded interval of positive length

examples.en: Our exercise uses a continuous uniform distribution with constant density between two endpoints.
examples.zh: 我们的习题使用了「连续均匀分布」，其两个端点之间的密度为常数。

examples.en: Equal-length intervals inside the support have equal probabilities under a continuous uniform distribution.
examples.zh: 在「连续均匀分布」下，支撑集内长度相同的区间概率相同。

collocations: continuous uniform distribution on an interval
sample from a continuous uniform distribution

words.enDefinition: One random trial with two categories designated success and failure

examples.en: The tutor treated one coin toss as a Bernoulli trial with two possible outcomes.
examples.zh: 老师把一次抛硬币视为有两种可能结果的「伯努利试验」。

examples.en: We labeled the outcomes before representing each draw as a Bernoulli trial.
examples.zh: 把每次抽取表示为一个「伯努利试验」之前，我们先为结果设置了标签。

words.enDefinition: Distribution assigning success probability to one and the remaining probability to zero

examples.en: The Bernoulli distribution models the variable that equals one when the light turns on.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，如果灯亮，「伯努利分布」对应的变量就取一。

examples.en: We represented one pass or fail result using a Bernoulli distribution in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂上用「伯努利分布」表示一次通过或未通过的结果。

words.enDefinition: Variable equal to one when a specified event occurs and zero otherwise

examples.en: We defined an indicator random variable that equals one when the first die shows six.
examples.zh: 我们定义了一个「示性随机变量」，当第一枚骰子掷出六点时它等于一。

examples.en: The expectation of an indicator random variable equals the probability of the corresponding event.
examples.zh: 「示性随机变量」的期望等于对应事件的概率。

collocations: expectation of an indicator random variable

words.enDefinition: Chance of the outcome designated as success on a single trial

examples.en: The model keeps the success probability fixed for every spin of the wheel.
examples.zh: 模型中，每次转动转盘的「成功概率」都固定不变。

examples.en: We changed the success probability when the spinner's target region became larger.
examples.zh: 转盘的目标区域变大后，我们改变了「成功概率」。

words.enDefinition: Distribution counting successes in a fixed number of independent trials with common probability

examples.en: We used a binomial distribution to count heads in twelve independent tosses of one coin.
examples.zh: 我们用「二项分布」表示同一枚硬币独立抛掷十二次时出现正面的次数。

examples.en: The binomial distribution needs both the trial count and the success probability as parameters.
examples.zh: 「二项分布」需要同时以试验次数和成功概率作为参数。

words.enDefinition: Distribution of trials to the first success with independent attempts and fixed probability

examples.en: The geometric distribution gives the number of tosses through the first head, including that final toss.
examples.zh: 「几何分布」给出直到首次出现正面所需的抛掷次数，含出现正面的那一次。

examples.en: Our geometric distribution counts the successful attempt as part of the total number.
examples.zh: 我们的「几何分布」将成功的那一次试验也计入总次数。

collocations: geometric distribution of a waiting count

words.enDefinition: Distribution of failures before a specified success count in independent identical trials

examples.en: We used a negative binomial distribution to model the number of tails before the third head.
examples.zh: 我们用「负二项分布」建模第三次出现正面前反面出现的次数。

examples.en: The negative binomial distribution in our worksheet stops when the experiment reaches a predetermined success count.
examples.zh: 习题中的「负二项分布」记录的是试验达到预先指定成功次数前的失败次数。

collocations: parameters of a negative binomial distribution
example of a negative binomial distribution

words.enDefinition: Distribution counting one type of item in fixed uniform draws without replacement

examples.en: A hypergeometric distribution describes how many red tiles appear when four are drawn without replacement.
examples.zh: 「超几何分布」描述不放回抽取四块牌时抽到红牌的数量。

examples.en: The tutor used a hypergeometric distribution because the remaining pool changed after each draw.
examples.zh: 因为每次抽取后剩下的牌都发生变化，老师采用了「超几何分布」。

words.enDefinition: Joint distribution of category counts across independent trials with fixed category probabilities

examples.en: We used a multinomial distribution to count each face across repeated independent rolls.
examples.zh: 我们用「多项分布」表示多次独立掷骰中各点数出现的次数。

examples.en: The counts under the multinomial distribution must sum to the total number of trials.
examples.zh: 「多项分布」中，各类计数之和必须等于试验总次数。

collocations: category probabilities in a multinomial distribution

words.enDefinition: A distribution on nonnegative integer counts whose probabilities are proportional to the mean raised to the count divided by the count factorial.

examples.en: The example uses a Poisson distribution for the count of arrivals within a fixed interval.
examples.zh: 该例用「泊松分布」表示在固定区间内观察到的到达次数。

examples.en: The mean and variance of a Poisson distribution both equal its parameter.
examples.zh: 「泊松分布」的均值和方差都等于其参数。

words.enDefinition: Approximation of many independent rare successes by a Poisson count distribution

examples.en: We used a Poisson approximation to the binomial when individual successes were rare and trials were numerous.
examples.zh: 当单次成功概率很低且试验次数很多时，我们使用了「二项分布的泊松近似」。

examples.en: The Poisson approximation to the binomial uses the expected success count as the mean of the approximating distribution.
examples.zh: 「二项分布的泊松近似」以期望成功次数作为泊松分布的均值。

collocations: use a Poisson approximation to the binomial
derive the Poisson approximation to the binomial
accuracy of the Poisson approximation to the binomial

words.enDefinition: Constant-rate counting process with independent increments and Poisson counts in each interval

examples.en: We modeled arrivals as a Poisson process with a constant average rate over time.
examples.zh: 我们将到达建模为平均到达率随时间保持不变的「泊松过程」。

examples.en: In the Poisson process, counts in disjoint intervals have independent probability distributions.
examples.zh: 在「泊松过程」中，不相交区间的计数在概率上相互独立。

collocations: model arrivals as a Poisson process

words.enDefinition: Average number of arrivals per time unit in a specified process

examples.en: The model doubles the arrival rate while keeping the observation window the same length.
examples.zh: 模型把「到达率」翻倍，同时保持观察时段长度不变。

examples.en: We used the arrival rate to calculate the expected count during half an hour.
examples.zh: 我们用「到达率」计算半小时内的期望到达次数。

words.enDefinition: Property that changes over disjoint time intervals are mutually independent

examples.en: Our model assumes independent increments, so separate times contribute independent counts to the total.
examples.zh: 我们模型假设存在「独立增量」，因此不同时段的计数相互独立并加总。

examples.en: We checked independent increments by examining the joint law of counts in disjoint intervals.
examples.zh: 我们通过考察不相交区间中计数的联合分布，检验「独立增量」。

words.enDefinition: Property that the distribution of a change depends only on interval length

examples.en: With stationary increments, two intervals of equal duration give the same distribution of changes.
examples.zh: 具有「平稳增量」时，两个等长区间内的变化量服从同一分布。

examples.en: We used stationary increments to shift the observation window while preserving its count distribution.
examples.zh: 我们利用「平稳增量」移动观察时段，同时保持该时段内计数的分布。

words.enDefinition: A continuous distribution on nonnegative values with an exponentially decreasing survival probability, used for waiting times between Poisson arrivals.

examples.en: The exponential distribution in our model gives the wait until the next arrival.
examples.zh: 我们的模型用「指数分布」表示等待下一次到达的时间。

examples.en: The mean waiting time under an exponential distribution is the reciprocal of its rate parameter.
examples.zh: 在「指数分布」下，平均等待时间是其速率参数的倒数。

words.enDefinition: Property where additional waiting has the original distribution after any elapsed wait

examples.en: Because of the memoryless property, the remaining wait has the same law after two minutes.
examples.zh: 由于具有「无记忆性」，等待两分钟后剩余等待时间的分布仍和原先相同。

examples.en: We checked the memoryless property by comparing a conditional waiting probability with its original counterpart.
examples.zh: 我们比较有条件的等待概率和原来的对应概率，检验「无记忆性」。

words.enDefinition: Positive continuous distribution family specified by a shape and rate or scale

examples.en: A gamma distribution modeled the total wait for several arrivals in our worksheet.
examples.zh: 习题用「伽马分布」对等待若干次到达所需的总时间建模。

examples.en: We compared the gamma distribution under two shape settings with the same scale.
examples.zh: 我们比较了尺度相同而形状参数不同的两个「伽马分布」。

words.enDefinition: Continuous probability family on zero to one defined by two shape parameters

examples.en: We chose a beta distribution because the modeled quantity was a proportion between zero and one.
examples.zh: 由于所建模的量是零到一之间的比例，我们选择了「贝塔分布」。

examples.en: The beta distribution becomes uniform when both shape parameters equal one in this formula.
examples.zh: 在这个公式中，当两个形状参数均为一时，「贝塔分布」变成均匀分布。

collocations: shape parameters of a beta distribution

words.enDefinition: Continuous bell-shaped distribution characterized by its mean and positive variance

examples.en: We fit a normal distribution to the simulated measurements for comparison with the histogram.
examples.zh: 我们用「正态分布」拟合模拟测量值，以便与直方图比较。

examples.en: In the example, increasing variance made the normal distribution wider around its mean.
examples.zh: 例子中，增加方差让「正态分布」在均值两侧变得更宽。

words.enDefinition: Normal distribution having a mean of zero and variance of one

examples.en: We converted the measurement cutoff to use the standard normal distribution for our probability calculation.
examples.zh: 我们换算了测量值的界限，以便使用「标准正态分布」计算概率。

examples.en: The standard normal distribution is centered at zero and has unit spread in our example.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，「标准正态分布」以零为中心，标准差为一。

collocations: quantile of the standard normal distribution
area under the standard normal distribution

words.enDefinition: Table of probabilities or quantiles for the mean-zero unit-variance normal distribution

examples.en: We read the standard normal table to find the cumulative probability below a given score.
examples.zh: 我们查阅「标准正态分布表」，求得低于所给标准分数的累积概率。

examples.en: The tutor identified which tail the standard normal table represented before we used its entries.
examples.zh: 老师先确认「标准正态分布表」中的数值对应哪个尾部，然后我们才使用这些数值。

collocations: look up a value in a standard normal table

words.enDefinition: Subtract its mean and divide by its positive standard deviation

examples.en: We learned to standardize a random variable so values from different scales would be comparable.
examples.zh: 我们学会了「将随机变量标准化」，使不同量表上的取值可以比较。

examples.en: To standardize a random variable, the worksheet supplies both its mean and standard deviation.
examples.zh: 为了「将随机变量标准化」，习题给出了它的均值和标准差。

collocations: standardize a random variable before comparing values
standardize a random variable using its mean
show how to standardize a random variable

words.enDefinition: Signed number of standard deviations separating a value from its mean

examples.en: The z-score was negative because the recorded wait was below its mean.
examples.zh: 由于记录下的等待时间比均值短，「标准分数」为负。

examples.en: We calculated a z-score to compare the two measurements on a common scale.
examples.zh: 我们计算「标准分数」，用同一尺度比较这两个测量值。

collocations: convert a value to a z-score

words.enDefinition: Use of a normal curve to estimate binomial probabilities when conditions permit

examples.en: We compared the normal approximation to the binomial with exact binomial probabilities in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们在习题中将「二项分布的正态近似」与精确的二项概率作了比较。

examples.en: The tutor checked expected success and failure counts before using the normal approximation to the binomial.
examples.zh: 老师在使用「二项分布的正态近似」前，检查了成功和失败的期望次数。

collocations: use the normal approximation to the binomial
accuracy of a normal approximation to the binomial
check conditions for the normal approximation to the binomial

words.enDefinition: Adjustment moving integer cutoffs by half a unit when using continuous approximations

examples.en: We used a continuity correction to approximate the probability of exactly seven successes.
examples.zh: 我们使用「连续性修正」近似计算恰好成功七次的概率。

examples.en: The continuity correction placed the upper boundary half a unit past the last included count.
examples.zh: 「连续性修正」将上边界放到最后一个纳入计数再往后半个单位的位置。

collocations: normal approximation with a continuity correction

words.enDefinition: Positive distribution obtained by exponentiating a normally distributed random variable

examples.en: We modeled positive durations with a lognormal distribution to allow an extended right tail.
examples.zh: 我们用「对数正态分布」对正的持续时间建模，使分布可以有较长的右尾。

examples.en: Taking logarithms of values from a lognormal distribution gives a normal distribution in theory.
examples.zh: 在理论上，对服从「对数正态分布」的变量取对数会得到正态分布。

words.enDefinition: Continuous symmetric distribution with heavy tails and no defined mean or variance

examples.en: The Cauchy distribution illustrates why a symmetric distribution can lack a defined mean.
examples.zh: 「柯西分布」说明为什么对称分布也可能没有定义良好的均值。

examples.en: We simulated a Cauchy distribution to examine the effect of very large observations.
examples.zh: 我们模拟了「柯西分布」，以考察非常大的观测值所产生的影响。

collocations: heavy tails of a Cauchy distribution

words.enDefinition: Parameter shifting a distribution along its scale without changing its shape

examples.en: We changed the location parameter and watched the whole curve slide to the right.
examples.zh: 我们改变「位置参数」，观察整条曲线向右移动。

examples.en: The location parameter is the mean for the normal family used in our model.
examples.zh: 在我们模型所用的正态分布族中，「位置参数」就是均值。

words.enDefinition: Positive parameter stretching or compressing a distribution along its measurement scale

examples.en: Increasing the scale parameter made the probability curve broader in our classroom example.
examples.zh: 在课堂例子中，增加「尺度参数」使概率曲线变得更宽。

examples.en: We held the scale parameter fixed while moving the center of the distribution.
examples.zh: 我们在移动分布中心时保持「尺度参数」不变。

words.enDefinition: Parameter altering a distribution's profile beyond shifting or uniformly rescaling it

examples.en: A different shape parameter gave the curve a different degree of asymmetry.
examples.zh: 另一个「形状参数」值使曲线的不对称程度发生变化。

examples.en: We changed the shape parameter while leaving the scale fixed in the model.
examples.zh: 我们改变「形状参数」，同时在模型中保持尺度固定。

collocations: shape parameter of a gamma distribution

words.enDefinition: Proportion of observed trials on which the event actually occurred

examples.en: We recorded the relative frequency of an event after ten, fifty, and one hundred repeated trials.
examples.zh: 我们分别在重复试验十次、五十次和一百次后记录了「事件的相对频率」。

examples.en: The relative frequency of an event varied more noticeably across small batches of tosses in class.
examples.zh: 在课堂上，每组抛掷次数较少时，组间的「事件的相对频率」波动更明显。

collocations: calculate the relative frequency of an event
compare the relative frequency of an event
record the relative frequency of an event

words.enDefinition: Result that averages of repeated observations approach their expected value under conditions

examples.en: The law of large numbers explains why the mean of many independent fair rolls approaches its expectation.
examples.zh: 「大数定律」说明了为什么多次独立掷公平骰子的平均点数会趋近其期望。

examples.en: We used the law of large numbers to discuss long-run frequencies in the coin model.
examples.zh: 我们用「大数定律」讨论硬币模型中的长期频率。

collocations: apply the law of large numbers
illustrate the law of large numbers
hypotheses of the law of large numbers

words.enDefinition: Bound on a nonnegative variable's upper tail using its mean and threshold

examples.en: We used Markov's inequality to bound the chance of exceeding a positive threshold.
examples.zh: 我们用「马尔可夫不等式」给超过一个正阈值的概率定出上界。

examples.en: The theorem sheet requires a nonnegative variable before we apply Markov's inequality.
examples.zh: 定理讲义要求变量非负，才能应用「马尔可夫不等式」。

collocations: bound a probability using Markov's inequality

words.enDefinition: Bound on deviations from the mean using variance and the chosen distance

examples.en: We applied Chebyshev's inequality after computing the mean and variance of the count.
examples.zh: 求出计数的均值和方差后，我们应用了「切比雪夫不等式」。

examples.en: The example uses Chebyshev's inequality to bound the chance of being far from average.
examples.zh: 这个例子用「切比雪夫不等式」给明显偏离均值的概率定出上界。

collocations: use Chebyshev's inequality to bound a tail

words.enDefinition: Result that averages converge in probability to their common mean under conditions

examples.en: By the weak law of large numbers, the chance of exceeding any fixed error threshold tends to zero.
examples.zh: 「弱大数定律」说明，随着试验次数增多，偏差超过给定阈值的概率会趋近零。

examples.en: We proved the weak law of large numbers for independent identically distributed observations with finite variance.
examples.zh: 我们对具有有限方差的独立同分布观测值证明了「弱大数定律」。

collocations: apply the weak law of large numbers
prove the weak law of large numbers
example of the weak law of large numbers

words.enDefinition: Result that sample averages converge to their mean almost surely under conditions

examples.en: The strong law of large numbers says the averages converge to the mean with probability one.
examples.zh: 「强大数定律」说明，平均值以概率一收敛到期望值。

examples.en: The textbook uses the strong law of large numbers for independent identically distributed outcomes with finite mean.
examples.zh: 教材将「强大数定律」用于期望有限的独立同分布结果。

collocations: apply the strong law of large numbers
prove the strong law of large numbers
assumptions for the strong law of large numbers

words.enDefinition: Errors exceed each fixed positive threshold with probability tending to zero

examples.en: To establish convergence in probability, we bounded the probability of an error exceeding a fixed threshold.
examples.zh: 为证明「依概率收敛」，我们给误差超过固定阈值的概率定出上界。

examples.en: Our example demonstrates convergence in probability as larger deviations become less likely with more observations.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，观测次数增加时，超出指定偏差的概率趋近零，体现了「依概率收敛」。

collocations: convergence in probability to a constant

words.enDefinition: Convergence along outcomes belonging to an event of probability one

examples.en: The almost sure convergence result holds along all paths except a set of probability zero.
examples.zh: 「几乎必然收敛」的结论对一个零概率集合之外的所有路径成立。

examples.en: We compared almost sure convergence with convergence in probability in two repeated experiment models.
examples.zh: 我们在两个重复试验模型中比较了「几乎必然收敛」和依概率收敛。

words.enDefinition: Convergence of distribution functions at all continuity points of the limiting distribution function

examples.en: The proof shows convergence in distribution by checking where the limiting cumulative function is continuous.
examples.zh: 证明通过检查极限累积分布函数的各个连续点，说明了「依分布收敛」。

examples.en: The histograms illustrate convergence in distribution toward a normal curve as the number of terms grows.
examples.zh: 直方图展示了随着项数增加，分布如何「依分布收敛」到正态分布。

collocations: convergence in distribution to a normal law

words.enDefinition: Probability law approached by a sequence of distributions in a specified sense

examples.en: The limiting distribution in our example is normal after centering and scaling the sums.
examples.zh: 在我们的例子中，和经过中心化和缩放后，「极限分布」为正态分布。

examples.en: We evaluated the limiting distribution at a continuity point to compare probabilities.
examples.zh: 我们在一个连续点求「极限分布」的累积概率，以比较两种概率。

words.enDefinition: Condition that the expectation of a variable's square is finite

examples.en: We verified that each draw had a finite second moment before applying the theorem.
examples.zh: 在应用定理前，我们先确认每次抽样得到的随机变量都有「有限二阶矩」。

examples.en: The model's variable has a finite second moment because it takes values within fixed bounds.
examples.zh: 该模型的变量具有「有限二阶矩」，因为它的值始终在固定的界内。

collocations: check for a finite second moment

words.enDefinition: Result giving an asymptotically normal law for standardized sums under suitable conditions

examples.en: The central limit theorem applies here to independent, identically distributed draws with finite positive variance.
examples.zh: 我们将「中心极限定理」用于方差为正且有限的独立同分布变量之和。

examples.en: The central limit theorem supports a normal approximation even when each draw is distinctly asymmetric.
examples.zh: 即使每次抽样的分布明显不对称，「中心极限定理」也能支持使用正态近似。

collocations: assumptions of the central limit theorem

words.enDefinition: Sum with its mean subtracted, then divided by its positive standard deviation

examples.en: We formed a standardized sum before comparing its distribution with the standard normal curve.
examples.zh: 我们先求出「标准化的和」，再将其分布与标准正态曲线比较。

examples.en: In our exercise, the standardized sum has mean zero and variance one.
examples.zh: 习题中的「标准化的和」均值为零，方差为一。
